children: Brent crude fell to $104.4 a barrel on Wednesday, as markets weighed disruptions to Saudi supply.

Satellite imagery and industry sources indicated that three pumping stations serving Saudi Arabia’s vital East-West Pipeline were damaged in last week’s attack, one more than previously assessed, while the repair timeline remains uncertain.
Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen exchanged fresh strikes across their border on Thursday, while civilians fled by boat across the Red Sea as fighting spread.
Saudi Aramco has also informed at least two European refining customers that they will receive no crude next month following the attack on the key pipeline to the Red Sea.
Meanwhile, China’s refined oil product exports rose 12.7% year on year in August, with jet fuel exports reaching a record high.
Further easing of export controls in September could allow Chinese refiners to benefit from stronger overseas margins.
Brent is up for the third week.

title: Brent Crude Falls on Friday
